HVAC CONTROLS LAB / VIRTUAL SENSOR BENCH
=======================================

RUN THE KIT
1. Extract the entire ZIP. On the laptop connected to the isolated bench
   network, run Start-TM172-Bench.cmd (Python 3.9+). On macOS/Linux, run
   python3 start_bench.py. The bridge uses the Python standard library.
2. Keep physical equipment disconnected. Enable the PLC's Ethernet and
   Modbus TCP server. Use the actual private IPv4 address, unit ID, and
   the bench laptop's matching subnet. The bridge uses TCP port 502.
3. The local app opens in your browser. Enter the mapping described below.
   Save map creates a local JSON file for reuse with the same project.

CREATE THE PLC MAP
Use a bench copy of the EcoStruxure Machine Expert – HVAC project. Under
Configuration > Modbus Objects > Status Variables, create single-word
signed INT tags with scale 1 and offset 0. Record each project's Address
column value. Enter those one-based numbers in the bench. The bridge
subtracts one on the wire. Avoid HMI address prefixes. Use dedicated
Status Variables for test writes.

  Writable input value: Sim_SAT, Sim_RH, Sim_Static, Sim_FilterDP, etc.
  Writable digital value: Sim_FanProof, Sim_Occupied, Sim_FreezeOK, etc.
  Optional writable quality: Sim_SAT_Good (1 good, 0 bad).
  Writable heartbeat: BenchHeartbeat (unique signed INT, range 0..32767).
  Read-only command mirror: Bench_FanRun (0 or 1) or Bench_FanSpeedCmd
  (e.g. 0..1000 raw for a 0.0..100.0 percent speed reference).

Set each INT's allowed range to include its raw test values. A digital
contact writes 0 for open and 1 for closed. Choose tag names and apply
polarity according to your existing logic. An analog value is multiplied
by counts per unit and rounded to a signed INT. For example, 72.5 °F with
10 counts per unit sends 725. Set the PLC conversion to divide by the same
factor. All test values, quality words, and heartbeat must have unique
addresses. Command mirrors can be shared as read-only inputs to the bench.

PLC SELECTOR
Use TM172-Selector.st as a starting point. Declare the non-retentive
selector variables in your project, link BenchPermit_Local to a PLC-local
bench control that starts OFF, and call the selector each scan before the
sequence. Keep the real input scaling and hardwired safety circuits
functional. Use the effective temperature, quality, and contact values
in the testable sequence. Confirm the exact tags, units, ranges, polarity,
initialization, and fallback behavior in your project before downloading.

Each verified bench scan advances the heartbeat. The example copies the
new values on that heartbeat edge so the logic sees a verified snapshot.
With the example watchdog, the PLC returns to its physical input path after
six seconds without a fresh heartbeat. Turn off the PLC-local permit at
the end of every test. Closing or stopping the app leaves the last test
words in the controller. A Stop request ends future scans after any
in-flight scan. The PLC watchdog controls when the simulated values stop
being selected.

WORK THROUGH THE FIRST TEST
1. Leave the PLC-local permit OFF. Map one sensor, one heartbeat, and any
   feedback or quality addresses in the local app.
2. Click Read project map. This reads registers without writing. Compare
   the addresses and values with Online Watch. A successful read verifies
   communication, while the project and Online Watch establish tag identity.
3. Confirm the isolated bench and start a test. Watch raw values and the
   heartbeat change in Online Watch. Enable the PLC-local permit and
   verify BenchActive and the effective sensor values.
4. Test loss of communication. Stop the test and confirm BenchActive
   drops when the watchdog expires. Then turn the local permit OFF.

CHANNEL BEHAVIORS
Manual: use the slider, numeric value, or contact button while running.
Timed profile: rows contain seconds, value, step/ramp, and good/bad. Start
at zero. Each ramp ends at that row's time and starts at the previous
row. A step applies at its specified time. Digital profiles use steps.
A bad-quality row requires a mapped quality word. A profile holds its
last value until Stop. Example for a supply temperature sensor:
    0, 55, step, good
    12, 65, ramp, good
    20, 65, step, bad
    30, 55, step, good

PLC command: a digital contact follows a zero/nonzero command with
separate on/off delays and optional inversion. An analog response maps
the command's raw low/high values to sensor min/max, with optional lag.
Force manual value can temporarily override a timed or following point.
With a quality word mapped, Sensor good can inject an invalid signal
independently from the value. A mapped quality word tests the PLC
application's bad-sensor logic downstream of the physical input.

Example: map Supply fan proof to Sim_FanProof and follow Bench_FanRun
with 2 seconds on delay. When the PLC requests the fan, the bench returns
proof. During the run, force a manual open contact to test loss of proof.

The kit supports up to 16 mapped sensors. It verifies writes by reading
the test words, writes changed values, and advances the heartbeat only
after their readback succeeds. A protocol error, readback mismatch, or
lost browser connection stops the run. Use a new map read before restarting.
